sentences.text: With the consent of parties, the matter is heard finally.

2. This appeal under section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 has been filed by the Shanti Vishwakarma vs Surendra Singh Thakur on 16 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/155676420/
1 appellant/claimant being dissatisfied by the award dated 19.12.2022 passed by 5th Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Katni (hereinafter referred to as the "Tribunal") in Claim Case No.114/2020 whereby the Tribunal has awarded compensation of Rs.75,000/- and prayed for enhancement by a further sum of Rs.2,00,000/-.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 3. Brief facts of the case are that on 06.1.2020 the appellant while she was going from her home to field and as soon as she reached ahead Bus Stand at that juncture a motorcycle bearing registration No.MP-21/MM-7211 coming from Patori driven by respondent No.1 dashed against appellant as a result of which she sustained injuries in her right leg and various other parts of body.
She filed claim petition claiming compensation of Rs.7,70,000/-.

The Tribunal holding that accident occurred due to negligence of respondent No.1 in which appellant sustained injuries but the same did not cause any permanent disablement and accordingly, granted total compensation of Rs.75,000/-.

Hence,
this appeal for enhancement of compensation by Rs.2,00,000/- by paying court fees of Rs.5,000/-.
4. The accident, negligence and liability are not in dispute, therefore, findings of the Tribunal in that regard are not under assail.

5. Learned counsel for the appellant assails the impugned award on the ground that no amount has been granted for permanent disablement as per observations in paragraphs 23 & 25 of the award and also not awarded any amount towards loss of earning.

It is further submitted that no proper compensation has been granted towards pain & suffering, loss of income, loss of amenities of life due to disablement and hence, the compensation be suitably enhanced.
6. Learned counsel for the respondent/Insurance Company has supported the impugned award and claimed dismissal of instant appeal.
Although learned counsel for Insurance Company being officer of the Court fairly submits that no amount has been granted specifically for fracture, loss of earning and future treatment.

He further submits that fracture is something different and is basically of permanent nature in the sense that even when healed the pain remains to some extent although its percentage may vary, therefore,
compensation under this head can be granted.
7. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the Tribunal.
Considering the oral and documentary evidence available on record, it appears that Tribunal has not granted any amount towards fracture, loss of earning and future treatment.
The Tribunal has awarded compensation on lower side under heads viz fracture, attendant, special diet, transportation.

Therefore, in the facts and circumstances of the case, it would be just and proper that for fracture to grant/enhancement Rs.45,000/- towards facture; Rs.15,000/- is enhanced towards special diet, attendant and transportation; loss of income during treatment is assessed and awarded at Rs.15,000/- and towards future treatment Rs.10,000/- is awarded.
Hence, the total amount of compensation is enhanced by Rs.85,000/-.
The appellant would be entitled to interest over the enhanced amount of compensation as awarded by the Tribunal.
8. With the aforesaid modification in the impugned award, the appeal is allowed in part.
